text: BrainVision file format EEG recording BrainVision Core Data Format consists three separate files: Header file (.vhdr): text file containing recording parameters meta-information. Marker file (.vmrk): text file describing events collected EEG data recording. Raw EEG data file (.eeg): binary file containing EEG data well additional signals recorded along EEG (e.g. EOG). BrainVision files can imported R, example, using import_raw() function eegUtils package (available GitHub): details eegUtils package, visit official documentation: https://craddm.github.io/eegUtils/. HDF5 file format HD-EEG data exported MATLAB often stored HDF5 (Hierarchical Data Format version 5) file format. binary, platform-independent format designed efficient storage access large complex datasets. Data organized hierarchical structure, similar file system. R environment, rhdf5 hdf5r packages available working HDF5 files. following, present example using H5Fopen() function rhdf5 package.
code: # Install eegUtils from GitHub if not already installed # install.packages("remotes") # remotes::install_github("craddm/eegUtils") library(eegUtils)  # Import data from a BrainVision .vhdr file FILE_VHDR <- "name_of_the_eeg_data_file.vhdr" PATH <- "the complete path to the file" data_eeg <- eegUtils::import_raw(FILE_VHDR, file_path = PATH) # Install rhdf5 if not already installed # install.packages("BiocManager") # BiocManager::install("rhdf5") library("rhdf5")  # Import data from a HDF5 file PATH <- "the complete path to the file" data_eeg <- rhdf5::H5Fopen(PATH)

Example HDF5 files Assume , using procedure described Step 2, imported HDF5 file containing EEG data. stimulus-locked signal stored component denoted dataT, three-dimensional array dimensions number sensors × number time points × number epochs. assumptions, procedure converting stimulus-locked data one epoch long-format table may proceed follows: Notes: Unfortunately, MATLAB .mat files version 7.3 higher (HDF5-based), currently straightforward way read sensor labels directly R. However, code can readily adapted accommodate additional variables, different groups experimental conditions, present data.
code: signal_array <- data$dataT # array with signal values n_epoch <- dim(signal_array)[3] # number of epochs n_time <- dim(signal_array)[2] # number of time points n_sensor <- dim(signal_array)[1] # number of sensors  # create long-format table for epoch 01 df_stimul <- as.data.frame(t(signal_array[, , 1])) colnames(df_stimul) <- sensornames # vector with sensor labels data_epoch_01 <- tidyr::pivot_longer(   data = df_stimul,   cols = everything(),   values_to = "signal",   names_to = "sensor" ) n1 <- nrow(data_epoch_01)  # add epoch, subject and time numbers/IDs to the table data_epoch_01 <- data_epoch_01 |>   tibble::add_column(     subject = rep("subject_id", n1),     epoch = rep(1, n1),     time = rep(1:n_time, each = n_sensor)   )

.data$average[.data$subject == "2"]   ) # create colour scale CS1 <- create_scale(col_range = range(subjects_diff$diff), type = "redblue") # display the plot: positive difference values (i.e., average for subject 1 higher than for subject 2) # are displayed in shades of red, negative values in shades of blue topo_plot(subjects_diff, amplitude = "diff", mesh = M,           template = "HCGSN256", col_scale = CS1)

title: Dynamic and Interactive EEG Graphics
text: Overview diegr package enables researchers visualize high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) data animated interactive graphics, supporting exploratory confirmatory analyses sensor-level brain signals. package diegr includes: interactive boxplots (boxplot_epoch, boxplot_subject, boxplot_rt) interactive waveforms (interactive_waveforms) surface plots (interactive_surfaceplot, interactive_surfaceplot_curves) topographic maps 2D (topo_plot) scalp plots 3D (scalp_plot) functions computing summary statistics, baseline correction, pointwise jackknife means (summary_stats_rt,baseline_correction, compute_mean) functions easy selection data subsets regions interest (pick_data, pick_region) functions plotting mean pointwise confidence intervals (plot_time_mean, plot_topo_mean) animations time course raw signals averages 2D 3D (animate_topo, animate_topo_mean, animate_scalp)

title: Dynamic and Interactive EEG Graphics
text: Due large volumes data obtained HD-EEG measurements, package allows users work directly database tables (addition common formats data frames tibbles). approach much memory-efficient. database want use input diegr functions must contain columns following structure: group - group IDs, subject - subject IDs, sensor - sensor labels, epoch - epoch numbers, condition - experimental condition labels, time - numbers time points (sampling indices, ms), signal - EEG signal amplitude microvolts (functions, name column containing amplitude can customized arbitrarily). Note: necessary data contain variables, , must named according structure presented . can use check_structure() function, checks data structure prints inferred hierarchy. package includes several training datasets: epochdata: epoched HD-EEG data (anonymized short slice big HD-EEG study presented Madetko-Alster, 2025) 2 subjects 204 selected sensors 50 time points (measured using EGI HCGSN256 system), rtdata: response times (time stimulus presentation pressing button) experiment involving simple visual motor task (anonymized short slice big HD-EEG study presented Madetko-Alster, 2025) well datasets containing sensor position coordinates: HCGSN256: list Cartesian coordinates HD-EEG sensor positions 3D space scalp surface projection 2D space according EGI HCGSN256 template, biosemi128 biosemi256: lists Cartesian coordinates HD-EEG sensor positions 3D space scalp surface projection 2D space according BioSemi system 128 256 electrodes, system1005: list Cartesian coordinates HD-EEG sensor positions 3D space scalp surface projection 2D space according standard 10-05 system. information structure built-data see package vignette vignette("diegr", package = "diegr").

what: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
text: Calculate pointwise jackknife (leave-one-) average signal across temporal spatial domain together standard error pointwise confidence interval (CI) bounds. Pointwise averages can computed two ways: standard (un-weighted) default, weighted using values column specified weights_col. function computes average group, subject, sensor/time point, condition epoch level (according level parameter). option level = "epoch" epochs averaged etc. Function assumes pre-prepared data according chosen level.

title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
code: compute_mean(   data,   amplitude = "signal_base",   domain = c("time", "space"),   level = c("epoch", "condition", "sensor", "subject", "group"),   type = c("point", "jack"),   weights_col = NULL,   R = NULL,   alpha = 0.95 )

title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
text: data data frame, tibble database table input data, required columns: time sensor (according selected domain), column EEG amplitude specified argument amplitude columns corresponding selected level. amplitude character specifying name column input data EEG amplitude values. Default "signal_base" computing average baseline corrected signal. domain character specifying domain average computed. One "time" "space". Option "time" computes time-resolved average time point, whereas "space" computes space-resolved average sensor. level character specifying level average calculation. possible values "epoch","condition", "sensor", "subject" "group". See Details information. type character specifying method calculating average, "point" pointwise average "jack" jackknife leave-one-average. weights_col character specifying name column containing observation weights. NULL, un-weighted standard pointwise average computed. R number replications used bootstrap interval calculation. Required computing pointwise mean. Default value 1000. alpha number indicating confidence interval level. default value 0.95 95% confidence intervals.

title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
text: tibble resulting average CI bounds according chosen level, domain alpha arguments. statistics saved columns average computed average amplitude value, n number observations used average computing, se standard error mean, ci_low lower bound confidence interval ci_up upper bound confidence interval. Additionally, returned object carries "diegr_metadata" attribute metadata level domain used computing.

title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
text: function supports averaging different hierarchical levels data (using level argument): "epoch": averaging across epochs. Returns average curve (time domain) sensor array (space domain) combination grouping variables. "condition": averages across experimental conditions. "sensor": averages across sensors (space domain) time points (time domain). "subject": averages across subjects. "group": averages across groups subjects (highest aggregation level). function assumes input adapted desired level averaging (.e. epoch level epoch column must present data etc.). levels higher epochs, averages lower level assumed input data. Weighted vs un-weighted average (type = "point"): weights_col NULL, observation treated equally (weight = 1), producing standard un-weighted mean, standard errors (SE), CI. weights_col provided, weighted average computed using values specified column weights. SE CI computed based weighted variance. Computing standard error mean: type = "point", standard error computed sample standard deviation divided square root sample size standard mean weighted alternative (weights_col specified). type = "jack", standard error jackknife standard error mean (exact formula see Efron Tibshirani 1994). Computing point confidence intervals: average value, upper lower bounds point confidence interval also available. Setting type = "point" R: bounds computed using percentile method bootstrapping R replicates (can slow large amounts data). Setting type = "point" without specifying R: bounds computed using standard error mean approximation Student distribution. Setting type = "jack": bounds computed using jackknife standard error mean approximation Student t-distribution. Note: used method assumes equal variance symmetric distribution, may problematic small samples. Note: NAs amplitude, weights_col columns, corresponding rows ignored average calculation function prints warning message.

title: Calculate mean in temporal or spatial domain — compute_mean
text: Efron B., Tibshirani RJ. Introduction Bootstrap. Chapman & Hall/CRC; 1994.

title: Create colour scale used in topographic figures — create_scale
text: topographical palette (type = "topo") created according topographical colours: negative values correspond shades blue purple positive values shades green, yellow red. zero value variable always border blue green shades. red-blue palette (type = "redblue") negative values corresponding shades blue positive values corresponding shades red. default (symmetric = TRUE), guarantee true perceptual uniformity equal visual emphasis, provided col_range additionally automatically symmetrized around zero based maximum absolute value. example, input range c(-2, 5) internally expanded c(-5, 5). default redblue palette, symmetrization ensures equivalent positive negative amplitudes mapped identical color intensities. Furthermore, redblue palette strictly anchors zero-point neutral background color, preventing false perceptual boundaries. (Note legacy topo palette also symmetrized, retains characteristic blue-green transition zero). Setting symmetric = FALSE disables zero-centering expansion, may useful strictly unipolar data heavily skewed distributions, though sacrifices equal visual emphasis opposite polarities. compare results different subjects conditions, set col_range cases. Otherwise, colours assigned separately plot consistent . parameter k set default respect range col_range follows: k = 0.1 range \(\leq 30\), k = 0.03 range \(\geq 70\), k = 0.04 otherwise.

Example dataset contains amplitude values measured chosen 204 channels 50 time points (stimulus time point 10) 2 representative subjects (one patient one healthy control subject). total number 50 epochs subject, 14 (15) epochs selected sample dataset. data intended testing EEG preprocessing visualization methods.

title: Plot interactive waveform graph — interactive_waveforms
text: plotly object showing interactive time series signal according chosen level. Additionally, returned object carries "diegr_metadata" attribute metadata plot data details.

title: Plot interactive waveform graph — interactive_waveforms
text: input data frame database table must contain column time (column time point numbers) column EEG amplitude (average amplitude) specified argument amplitude. must also contain least one optional columns (according level parameter - "sensor" level column sensor required etc.):group - column group identifiers,subject - column subject IDs,sensor - column sensor labels,epoch - column epoch numbers. Note: average signals must pre-aggregated plotting higher grouping levels, example sensor level assumes mean sensor signal amplitude column (input data individual epochs together sensor level setting result mess output). Plotting confidence ribbon: plot confidence bands around average lines (CI = TRUE), input data must include ci_up ci_low columns (output tibble compute_mean function).

code: make_triangulation(mesh)

title: Make triangulation of 2D point mesh — make_triangulation
text: mesh data frame tibble named columns: x, y (required) index (optionally, missing, generated internally). optimally D2 element "mesh" object list structure uniformly spaced grid.

title: Make triangulation of 2D point mesh — make_triangulation
text: three column matrix indices vertices triangles. row represents one triangle, defined three vertex indices pointing rows input mesh.

title: Make triangulation of 2D point mesh — make_triangulation
text: type-Delaunay triangulation triangulation obtained drawing north-east diagonals subrectangles triangulated area. Due regularity input mesh (sense distances mesh points), simplified procedure used: triangulation created within individual strips bound together. order vertices chosen maintain consistent orientation triangles (details see Schneider 2003). input mesh regular grid spacing, result triangulation may meaningful meet Delaunay triangulation criteria.

triangulation on this mesh TRI <- make_triangulation(M$D2) head(TRI) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1   16   15 #> [2,]    1    2   16 #> [3,]    2   17   16 #> [4,]    2    3   17 #> [5,]    3   18   17 #> [6,]    3    4   18  # c) plot triangulation in 2D # prepare empty plot plot(M$D2, type = "n", main = "Triangulation plot", xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1, axes = FALSE) # create a structure for plotting x0 <- c() y0 <- c() x1 <- c() y1 <- c() for (i in 1:nrow(TRI)) {   v_indices <- TRI[i, ]   v_coords <- M$D2[v_indices, ]   x0 <- c(x0, v_coords[1, "x"], v_coords[2, "x"], v_coords[3, "x"])   y0 <- c(y0, v_coords[1, "y"], v_coords[2, "y"], v_coords[3, "y"])   x1 <- c(x1, v_coords[2, "x"], v_coords[3, "x"], v_coords[1, "x"])   y1 <- c(y1, v_coords[2, "y"], v_coords[3, "y"], v_coords[1, "y"])  } # plot triangulation using segments segments(x0, y0, x1, y1)   ## Note: this code opens a rgl 3D viewer # d) Plot the result triangulation as 3D wire model using rgl // File 1 is the vertex shader
#ifdef GL_ES
#ifdef GL_FRAGMENT_PRECISION_HIGH
precision highp float;
#else
precision mediump float;
#endif
#endif

attribute vec3 aPos;
attribute vec4 aCol;
uniform mat4 mvMatrix;
uniform mat4 prMatrix;
varying vec4 vCol;
varying vec4 vPosition;

#ifdef NEEDS_VNORMAL
attribute vec3 aNorm;
uniform mat4 normMatrix;
varying vec4 vNormal;
#endif

#if defined(HAS_TEXTURE) || defined (IS_TEXT)
attribute vec2 aTexcoord;
varying vec2 vTexcoord;
#endif

#ifdef FIXED_SIZE
uniform vec3 textScale;
#endif

#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
attribute vec3 aOfs;
#endif

#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
#ifdef HAS_NORMALS
varying float normz;
uniform mat4 invPrMatrix;
#else
attribute vec3 aPos1;
attribute vec3 aPos2;
varying float normz;
#endif
#endif // IS_TWOSIDED

#ifdef FAT_LINES
attribute vec3 aNext;
attribute vec2 aPoint;
varying vec2 vPoint;
varying float vLength;
uniform float uAspect;
uniform float uLwd;
#endif

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
varying vec3 vReflection;
#endif

void main(void) {
  
#ifndef IS_BRUSH
#if defined(NCLIPPLANES) || !defined(FIXED_QUADS) || defined(HAS_FOG) || defined(USE_ENVMAP)
  vPosition = mvMatrix * vec4(aPos, 1.);
#endif
  
#ifndef FIXED_QUADS
  gl_Position = prMatrix * vPosition;
#endif
#endif // !IS_BRUSH
  
#ifdef IS_POINTS
  gl_PointSize = POINTSIZE;
#endif
  
  vCol = aCol;
  
// USE_ENVMAP implies NEEDS_VNORMAL

#ifdef NEEDS_VNORMAL
  vNormal = normMatrix * vec4(-aNorm, dot(aNorm, aPos));
#endif

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
  vReflection = normalize(reflect(vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w, 
                        normalize(vNormal.xyz/vNormal.w)));
#endif
  
#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
#ifdef HAS_NORMALS
  /* normz should be calculated *after* projection */
  normz = (invPrMatrix*vNormal).z;
#else
  vec4 pos1 = prMatrix*(mvMatrix*vec4(aPos1, 1.));
  pos1 = pos1/pos1.w - gl_Position/gl_Position.w;
  vec4 pos2 = prMatrix*(mvMatrix*vec4(aPos2, 1.));
  pos2 = pos2/pos2.w - gl_Position/gl_Position.w;
  normz = pos1.x*pos2.y - pos1.y*pos2.x;
#endif
#endif // IS_TWOSIDED
  
#ifdef NEEDS_VNORMAL
  vNormal = vec4(normalize(vNormal.xyz), 1);
#endif
  
#if defined(HAS_TEXTURE) || defined(IS_TEXT)
  vTexcoord = aTexcoord;
#endif
  
#if defined(FIXED_SIZE) && !defined(ROTATING)
  vec4 pos = prMatrix * mvMatrix * vec4(aPos, 1.);
  pos = pos/pos.w;
  gl_Position = pos + vec4(aOfs*textScale, 0.);
#endif
  
#if defined(IS_SPRITES) && !defined(FIXED_SIZE)
  vec4 pos = mvMatrix * vec4(aPos, 1.);
  pos = pos/pos.w + vec4(aOfs,  0.);
  gl_Position = prMatrix*pos;
#endif
  
#ifdef FAT_LINES
  /* This code was inspired by Matt Deslauriers' code in 
   https://mattdesl.svbtle.com/drawing-lines-is-hard */
  vec2 aspectVec = vec2(uAspect, 1.0);
  mat4 projViewModel = prMatrix * mvMatrix;
  vec4 currentProjected = projViewModel * vec4(aPos, 1.0);
  currentProjected = currentProjected/currentProjected.w;
  vec4 nextProjected = projViewModel * vec4(aNext, 1.0);
  vec2 currentScreen = currentProjected.xy * aspectVec;
  vec2 nextScreen = (nextProjected.xy / nextProjected.w) * aspectVec;
  float len = uLwd;
  vec2 dir = vec2(1.0, 0.0);
  vPoint = aPoint;
  vLength = length(nextScreen - currentScreen)/2.0;
  vLength = vLength/(vLength + len);
  if (vLength > 0.0) {
    dir = normalize(nextScreen - currentScreen);
  }
  vec2 normal = vec2(-dir.y, dir.x);
  dir.x /= uAspect;
  normal.x /= uAspect;
  vec4 offset = vec4(len*(normal*aPoint.x*aPoint.y - dir), 0.0, 0.0);
  gl_Position = currentProjected + offset;
#endif
  
#ifdef IS_BRUSH
  gl_Position = vec4(aPos, 1.);
#endif

// File 2 is the fragment shader
#ifdef GL_ES
#ifdef GL_FRAGMENT_PRECISION_HIGH
precision highp float;
#else
precision mediump float;
#endif
#endif
varying vec4 vCol; // carries alpha
varying vec4 vPosition;
#if defined(HAS_TEXTURE) || defined (IS_TEXT)
varying vec2 vTexcoord;
uniform sampler2D uSampler;
#endif

#ifdef HAS_FOG
uniform int uFogMode;
uniform vec3 uFogColor;
uniform vec4 uFogParms;
#endif

#if defined(IS_LIT) && !defined(FIXED_QUADS)
varying vec4 vNormal;
#endif

#if NCLIPPLANES > 0
uniform vec4 vClipplane[NCLIPPLANES];
#endif

#if NLIGHTS > 0
uniform mat4 mvMatrix;
#endif

#ifdef IS_LIT
uniform vec3 emission;
uniform float shininess;
#if NLIGHTS > 0
uniform vec3 ambient[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 specular[NLIGHTS]; // light*material
uniform vec3 diffuse[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 lightDir[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool viewpoint[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool finite[NLIGHTS];
#endif
#endif // IS_LIT

#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
uniform bool front;
varying float normz;
#endif

#ifdef FAT_LINES
varying vec2 vPoint;
varying float vLength;
#endif

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
varying vec3 vReflection;
#endif

void main(void) {
  vec4 fragColor;
#ifdef FAT_LINES
  vec2 point = vPoint;
  bool neg = point.y < 0.0;
  point.y = neg ? (point.y + vLength)/(1.0 - vLength) :
                 -(point.y - vLength)/(1.0 - vLength);
#if defined(IS_TRANSPARENT) && defined(IS_LINESTRIP)
  if (neg && length(point) <= 1.0) discard;
#endif
  point.y = min(point.y, 0.0);
  if (length(point) > 1.0) discard;
#endif // FAT_LINES
  
#ifdef ROUND_POINTS
  vec2 coord = gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5);
  if (length(coord) > 0.5) discard;
#endif
  
#if NCLIPPLANES > 0
  for (int i = 0; i < NCLIPPLANES; i++)
    if (dot(vPosition, vClipplane[i]) < 0.0) discard;
#endif
    
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    vec3 n = vec3(0., 0., 1.);
#elif defined(IS_LIT)
    vec3 n = normalize(vNormal.xyz);
#endif
    
#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
    if ((normz <= 0.) != front) discard;
#endif

#ifdef IS_LIT
    vec3 eye = normalize(-vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
    vec3 lightdir;
    vec4 colDiff;
    vec3 halfVec;
    vec4 lighteffect = vec4(emission, 0.);
    vec3 col;
    float nDotL;
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    n = -faceforward(n, n, eye);
#endif
    
#if NLIGHTS > 0
    // Simulate two-sided lighting
    if (n.z < 0.0)
      n = -n;
    for (int i=0;i<NLIGHTS;i++) {
      colDiff = vec4(vCol.rgb * diffuse[i], vCol.a);
      lightdir = lightDir[i];
      if (!viewpoint[i]) {
        if (finite[i]) {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 1.)).xyz;
        } else {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 0.)).xyz;
        }
      }
      if (!finite[i]) {
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      } else {
        lightdir = normalize(lightdir - vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      }
      col = ambient[i];
      nDotL = dot(n, lightdir);
      col = col + max(nDotL, 0.) * colDiff.rgb;
      col = col + pow(max(dot(halfVec, n), 0.), shininess) * specular[i];
      lighteffect = lighteffect + vec4(col, colDiff.a);
    }
#else
    lighteffect.a = 1.;
#endif
    
#else // not IS_LIT
    vec4 colDiff = vCol;
    vec4 lighteffect = colDiff;
#endif
    
#ifdef IS_TEXT
    vec4 textureColor = lighteffect*texture2D(uSampler, vTexcoord);
#endif
    
#ifdef HAS_TEXTURE

// These calculations use the definitions from 
// https://docs.gl/gl3/glTexEnv

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
    float m = 2.0 * sqrt(dot(vReflection, vReflection) + 2.0*vReflection.z + 1.0);
    vec4 textureColor = texture2D(uSampler, vReflection.xy / m + vec2(0.5, 0.5));
#else
    vec4 textureColor = texture2D(uSampler, vTexcoord);
#endif

#ifdef TEXTURE_rgb

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(textureColor.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = lighteffect*vec4(textureColor.rgb, 1.);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.rgb) * lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb + textureColor.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif //TEXTURE_rgb
        
#ifdef TEXTURE_rgba

#ifdef TEXMODE_replace
// already done
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = lighteffect*textureColor;
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_decal
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.a)*lighteffect.rgb) +
                     textureColor.a*textureColor.rgb, 
                     lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.rgb) * lighteffect.rgb,
                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb + textureColor.rgb,
                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif
    
#endif //TEXTURE_rgba
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb, luminance);
#endif 

#if defined(TEXMODE_modulate) || defined(TEXMODE_blend) || defined(TEXMODE_add)
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a*luminance);
#endif
 
#endif // TEXTURE_alpha
    
// The TEXTURE_luminance values are not from that reference    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(luminance, luminance, luminance, lighteffect.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance
 
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(luminance, luminance, luminance, textureColor.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);

#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    
    fragColor = textureColor;

#elif defined(IS_TEXT)
    if (textureColor.a < 0.1)
      discard;
    else
      fragColor = textureColor;
#else
    fragColor = lighteffect;
#endif // HAS_TEXTURE
    
#ifdef HAS_FOG
    // uFogParms elements: x = near, y = far, z = fogscale, w = (1-sin(FOV/2))/(1+sin(FOV/2))
    // In Exp and Exp2: use density = density/far
    // fogF will be the proportion of fog
    // Initialize it to the linear value
    float fogF;
    if (uFogMode > 0) {
      fogF = (uFogParms.y - vPosition.z/vPosition.w)/(uFogParms.y - uFogParms.x);
      if (uFogMode > 1)
        fogF = mix(uFogParms.w, 1.0, fogF);
      fogF = fogF*uFogParms.z;
      if (uFogMode == 2)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF);
      // Docs are wrong: use (density*c)^2, not density*c^2
      // https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/master/src/mesa/swrast/s_fog.c#L58
      else if (uFogMode == 3)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF*fogF);
      fogF = clamp(fogF, 0.0, 1.0);
      gl_FragColor = vec4(mix(fragColor.rgb, uFogColor, fogF), fragColor.a);
    } else gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#else
    gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#endif // HAS_FOG

title: diegr 0.3.0
text: Added functions creating interactive surface plots checking data structure. Added new sensor templates: BioSemi 128, BioSemi 256, system 10-05. Updated graphical functions ensure compatibility new templates. Added metadata computing graphic functions. Changed default palette create_scale() perceptually uniform "redblue" scale added range symmetrization around zero. Updated dealing NA values within compute_mean(), outliers_epoch() baseline_correction(). Added fallback MASS::ginv() ill-conditioned interpolation matrices. Rewrote point_mesh() using sf instead sp package. Fixed bugs outliers_epoch(), timeline rendering animations baseline range examples documentation. Added static version outputs boxplots. Updated installation method development version README, edited troubleshooting section vignette.
